title: Teaching LLMs to Abstain across Languages via Multilingual Feedback

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM abstention and question-answering accuracy across 26 diverse languages categorized into high-, mid-, and low-resource tiers, and computing linguistic utility, demographic utility, and equity metrics (using the Gini coefficient) to measure performance disparities across these languages.

Analyzing performance gaps between high- and low-resource languages across different MMLU knowledge domains to identify West-centric knowledge biases (e.g., larger gaps in US/European history), and evaluating the effectiveness of feedback generated from culturally related language clusters derived from the World Value Survey.
